sources.title: Omnara agents/configuration
sources.finding: YAML/JSON config selects provider/model/tools, versioned profiles and skills. Product subagents have model overrides, messaging, parent return, depth/instance caps and shared machines. Project memory stores retain current files without history.

sources.title: Omnara agents/overview
sources.finding: Dashboard/CLI/API launch durable agent conversations; activity exposes running, waiting, idle, archived, processes and subagents. Wait requires no background work; stop retains conversation.

sources.title: Omnara agents/failure-handling
sources.finding: Postgres event state survives worker crashes; another worker resumes saved steps without automatic tool rerun. Model calls retry up to eight times; interrupted external tools have unknown outcomes. Approval state persists.

sources.title: Omnara machines/overview
sources.finding: Own laptop/VM or provider sandbox executes commands via outbound daemon. Agent state belongs to control plane. Offline execution host returns retryable errors and need not preserve a live command result.

sources.title: Omnara machines/pools
sources.finding: Managed Ubuntu machines include dev tools; own provider image/snapshot supported. Files/processes survive idle suspension until deletion. Project grants and pool maximum capacity are hard limits.

sources.title: Omnara organization/members
sources.finding: Org owner/admin/member and project admin/developer/operator/viewer have explicit permissions. Operators can launch, send input, resolve interactions and stop shared agents.

sources.title: Omnara organization/model-providers
sources.finding: API keys and custom compatible endpoints including local vLLM; project model grants and token/time limits. Presets OpenAI/Anthropic/OpenRouter are model providers, not CLI harnesses.

sources.title: Omnara tools/permissions
sources.finding: Built-in/custom tools default allow; MCP default ask. Config declares allow/ask/deny per tool; updates required to change permission policy.

sources.title: Omnara tools/mcp
sources.finding: Connect third-party MCP tools including bearer secrets and OAuth.

sources.title: Omnara tools/skills
sources.finding: Versioned SKILL.md packages load on demand and are shared through explicit project grants; latest revision resolves at each model call.

sources.title: Omnara events/sending-input
sources.finding: Queued/steering inputs can be reordered/canceled/promoted; config changes take effect on next model call. Inputs attribute authenticated users or project actors.

sources.title: Omnara events/artifacts
sources.finding: Immutable artifact IDs and digests reference uploaded media; downloadable timeline cards remain after execution-machine removal.

sources.title: Omnara events/webhooks
sources.finding: Event webhooks watch agent/profile/project, optionally sign payloads and retry up to ten minutes; deliveries may duplicate or arrive out of order.

sources.title: Omnara self-hosting/deployment
sources.finding: Full API/worker/maintenance/frontend deployment uses own Postgres, Redis, S3-compatible bucket and memory filesystem; Docker Compose supports local/production.

sources.title: Omnara self-hosting/configuration
sources.finding: OIDC login connectors include Google, Keycloak, Okta, Auth0, Azure and ZITADEL. Self-host configuration defines service/model/machine settings.

sources.title: Omnara introduction
sources.finding: Web interface, CLI, REST API and TypeScript SDK; open-source self-hostable platform under Apache 2.0.

sources.title: Omnara pricing
sources.finding: Full platform $0 with no seat fees. Own models/machines free; managed models provider rates; managed runtime $0.0414/GiB-hour and retention $0.20016/GiB/30 days. No card. SOC2 Type II observation period in progress.

sources.title: Omnara README
sources.locator: Quickstart (Omnara Cloud, Self-host); How it works; Features; FAQ
sources.finding: Omnara Cloud needs a sign-in at app.omnara.com; self-hosting runs with Docker Compose and a local sign-up. Workers run the agent loop and every step is saved in Postgres. The CLI, dashboard, REST API and SDK launch agents. An agent can use several machines and, if a laptop goes offline, continue in a sandbox and sync back with git. Workers call the project's configured model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, Bedrock, LiteLLM, Ollama or compatible endpoints). The dashboard shows tool calls; self-hosted history stays in your own Postgres. The FAQ says the API, CLI, SDK and config format are the same on Cloud and self-hosted, and Apache 2.0 applies.

sources.title: Omnara docs: Failure handling
sources.locator: Failure table; How recovery works; Model calls; Approvals, questions, and machines
sources.finding: Every step is saved to Postgres so another worker resumes from the last saved step; a worker holds a lease on one agent, renewed about every 30 seconds, and a worker that lost its lease cannot save. Model errors are retried up to eight times; deploys give work 20 seconds to drain; commands keep running when the worker dies; a command not accepted within five minutes fails and an offline machine is reported unreachable after 30 seconds; approvals wait indefinitely.

sources.title: Omnara docs: Concepts
sources.finding: Omnara runs the agent loop and runtime for each configured agent; users interact by reading or streaming its event log, sending inputs and resolving questions and approvals.

sources.title: Omnara docs: Integrations
sources.locator: Select capabilities independently; Route questions and approvals
sources.finding: Slack and Discord integrations can supply an interaction handler that presents an agent's questions and approvals in the assigned conversation; the dashboard remains available if provider delivery fails.

sources.title: Omnara docs: Event webhooks
sources.finding: Project event webhooks deliver selected agent event types (agent_input, model_output, tool_result, context_checkpoint, tool_call_update) to a URL, including permission interaction updates.

sources.title: Omnara frontend/apps/web/package.json
sources.finding: The only frontend app is a React web app built with Vite; no service-worker or push-notification API use was found in frontend sources (searched PushManager, serviceWorker, Notification.requestPermission).

sources.title: Omnara docs: Architecture
sources.finding: The web process serves the compiled single-page application; the api process serves /api routes.

sources.title: Omnara docs: GitHub
sources.locator: Connect your GitHub App; PR tools; Git credentials
sources.finding: A user-owned GitHub App (guided registration for GitHub.com) gives agents PR tools (read, discussion and review comments, replies, start/submit/discard review, resolve threads) and HTTPS Git/gh credentials on github.com. Credentials are read-only unless 'Let agents push code' is enabled and can be limited to repository_ids; pushes stay subject to GitHub rules and cannot change .github/workflows. Human PR discussion, review input and new commits steer the agent; PR-open, mention launches and steering comments require repository write access.

sources.title: Omnara docs: Authentication
sources.finding: The Omnara API is exposed as an MCP server at https://app.omnara.com/mcp with browser OAuth sign-in for MCP clients such as Claude Code and Codex.

sources.title: Omnara internal/httpapi/routes.go
sources.finding: The API server mounts the MCP handler at /mcp, so self-hosted API deployments expose the same MCP endpoint.

sources.title: Omnara docs: Configs & profiles
sources.locator: Immutable configs; secret_env_overlay; Subagents; Advance a profile to a new config
sources.finding: Configs are immutable and a changed source gets a new config ID; profile updates advance a generation and keep previous versions in history. secret_env_overlay injects project secrets into agent processes, OMNARA_ names are reserved, and revoked secrets are omitted. Subagents spawned with spawn_agent are full agents managed with read_agent, send_agent_message, stop_agent and list_agents, nesting up to max_depth (default 1, at most 8).

sources.title: Omnara docs: Sending input
sources.locator: Attach files and images; Queued vs steering; Change the config mid-conversation; Actors and attribution
sources.finding: Inputs can attach images, PDFs, text files, spreadsheets and Office documents; steering messages arrive at the next model call; a running agent's config (model, tools, permissions, instructions) can be changed through the API without restarting; every input is attributed to the authenticated caller or a named actor.

sources.title: Omnara docs: Members & access
sources.finding: Project operators (and owners/admins) can operate agents: launch, send inputs, resolve interactions and stop work for any agent in the project.

sources.title: Omnara docs: Machines overview
sources.locator: Two ways to get one; Machine state
sources.finding: BYO machines are user-managed; pool machines are created on demand and deleted when released or after a configured idle period. When a machine goes offline a process may continue, but the agent cannot interact with it until the daemon reconnects; waiting tool calls return a retryable error after a grace period.

sources.title: Omnara docs: Machine pools
sources.finding: A pool machine keeps files, installed dependencies and running processes across turns, including across provider suspend/resume. It is deleted on delete_machine, pool deletion or after the idle period (at least 5 minutes, 0 disables); conversation, events and artifacts remain.

sources.title: Omnara docs: Streaming events
sources.locator: Read the timeline; What each event carries
sources.finding: Each agent's timeline lists ordered events (inputs, model outputs with requested tool calls, tool results with succeeded/failed/denied/canceled outcomes) by turn, readable through GET /events or a live stream.

sources.title: Omnara api/openapi/openapi.yaml
sources.finding: Event and turn paths expose only GET operations; there is no API to edit or delete agent events. Usage endpoints return model calls, tokens and cost totals by model for an agent (optionally including subagents), profile, project and organization, plus day/week/month timeseries.

sources.title: Omnara docs: Agents
sources.finding: Archiving stops work and releases machines, but the agent's event history remains available by ID.

sources.title: Omnara pricing
sources.finding: Omnara Cloud has a $0 platform fee and no per-seat fees; managed models bill at provider token rates and managed machines at $0.0414 per GiB of memory per hour online plus $0.20016 per GiB per 30 days retained, with idle machines auto-sleeping. BYO keys and machines are free, self-hosting is free, no credit card is required, and credits carry a 5% service fee. Accepted startups get credits for models and machines (amount not stated); Enterprise is by contact.
